Entry requirements · 2027 entry

Business Administration BSBA (Kenan-Flagler) at UNC Chapel Hill

What UNC Chapel Hill asks of applicants to Business Administration BSBA (Kenan-Flagler) for 2027 entry (the 2026–27 application cycle). Each requirement below is labelled verified, partly verified or not verified, with the date it was checked and a link to the official source.

US · All UNC Chapel Hill courses · Business field guide

Entry requirements 2027 entry 7 of 8 verified
SAT / ACT
  • SAT/ACT not required for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above (4.0 scale) — 2026–27 applications and beyond
  • Applicants with a weighted GPA below 2.8 must submit ACT 17+ or SAT 930+ (UNC System minimum)
  • If the school gives no 4.0 weighted GPA, an above-B+ average means no test is required; for Cambridge-based systems, A-level or external exam grades are used for this rule

UNC’s admissions pages apply to all first-year applicants; intended major does not affect admission.

Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: First-Year Application · UNC: Applying as an International First-Year Student
English language
  • Applicants without U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status are asked to submit English proficiency exam scores (listed as a required material for international first-year applicants)
  • Accepted: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, Cambridge English C1 Advanced, Cambridge C2 Proficiency

UNC publishes the scores strong applicants typically achieve and states they are not minimums, so no score is shown as a requirement.

Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: Applying as an International First-Year Student · UNC: Applying as an International First-Year Student
Admissions tests

None listed on the official source

Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: First-Year Application · UNC: How does UNC look at supplemental test scores?
Subject prerequisites
  • Not used in Altiora’s matching yet — see the note for the official guidance

Official: UNC System minimum high-school coursework to be eligible to apply — 4 units English; 4 units college-preparatory mathematics (e.g. algebra I and II, geometry and one unit beyond algebra II); 3 units science (one life/biological, one physical, one laboratory course); 2 units social science (one in U.S. history); 2 additional units of English, mathematics, science, social studies, world languages or computer science. Two sequential world language courses are recommended. Applicants who lack units may still apply and explain their circumstances. No major-specific high-school subjects are stated.

A-Level requirements
Grades
Not recorded
Details
Applicants from British-based systems need to have completed A Levels before enrolling; send exam scores such as GCSEs with the transcript. For Cambridge-based systems, A-level or external exam grades are used for the UNC System GPA-based testing rule.

No A-Level grade offer is stated.

Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: International curriculum and minimum course requirements (FAQ) · UNC: Applying as an International First-Year Student
IB requirements
Overall score
Not recorded
Details
IB exam scores are not required; applicants may self-report them. UNC encourages taking available IB, AP or dual-enrollment courses and states no preference between these programmes.

UNC’s pages checked do not say how the IB Diploma or predicted IB scores are treated in admission; no IB points figure is stated.

Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: How does UNC look at supplemental test scores? · UNC: Becoming a Tar Heel
Other qualifications
  • AP scores are not required; applicants may self-report them if they reflect their mastery of the material
Verified19 Oct 2026UNC: How does UNC look at supplemental test scores?
Other requirements
  • No direct entry to the BSBA as a first-year: high school applicants can be offered Assured Enrollment, otherwise students apply as current UNC students (intra-university transfer) after their first year
  • Assured Enrollment: apply by the Early Action deadline, select Assured Enrollment to UNC Kenan-Flagler under Special Opportunities, write a short supplemental essay, and list Business Administration among your top three academic interests
  • Assured Enrollment students enter the major in the fall of sophomore year if they stay in good standing and earn C or better in first-year calculus, statistics and BUSI 100
  • One letter of recommendation from a teacher in a core academic area (general UNC requirement)
